department: Department of Earth and Environmental Sciences

deadline.value: Submit by December 15 (competition for admission and aid).
deadline.quote: Because of competition for admission and financial aid, applications should be submitted by December 15.

app_fee.quote: There is a $70 application fee for applying to the Department of Earth and Environmental Sciences (EES) graduate programs.

gre_general.value: GRE scores are recommended but not required.
gre_general.quote: Graduate Record Examination (GRE) scores. (recommended, but not required)

supervisor.value: Identify faculty you want to work with and contact them about availability before applying.
supervisor.quote: please identify faculty members with whom you would be interested in doing research and contact them to check about availability prior to applying.

funding.value: PhD students are normally supported for five years with a full tuition scholarship, via assistantships and fellowships.
funding.quote: Normally, PhD students are supported for five years, and receive a full tuition scholarship. | Financial aid is available in the form of teaching and research assistantships and fellowships.

entry_route.value: A STEM degree is generally expected; the page does not say whether a master's is needed.
entry_route.quote: Applicants are generally expected to have degree in a STEM field with basic training in geology, environmental science or a related field

gre_subject.value: No GRE Subject test applies to this field and the page does not mention one.

notes: Listed as Geosciences in the university program list; the department is Earth and Environmental Sciences.
